posts.name: Shoaib Sadiq Salehmohamed
posts.cooked:
I have noticed in the lectures present in our course portal, in multiple lectures sir has refered topics and things that were not covered in the lectures present in the portal.

(Just as an example in L3.1 - Combining commands and files sir has mentioned return values of commands, which I felt were not a part of the previously covered lectures of week1 and week2.)

I then tried to confirm if I was missing out something, also cross checked the course portal just in case I have missed out some lectures, but still was unable to find anything.
I have also noticed it for other topics like sir mentioning that he has covered regular expressions in previous lectures while explaining editors in week2 etc.

I then tried to go through the course youtube playlist just to realise that there were many video’s before the lectures covering the topics present in the course portal.

I would request someone to please help me out and let us know what all lectures and things are needed to be covered to be upto speed before the lectures on the course portal.

I’m sorry if I am missing out on something that’s needed to be done before the lectures.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked: Lectures are restructured, earlier they were in different order

posts.name: Shoaib Sadiq Salehmohamed
posts.cooked:
Yes but how can I prevent myself from feeling lost when I am not able to understand certain things when sir is explaining. Could you please give some advice regarding how to catch up to things like regex etc coz I feel I’m not able to understand when sir is using then.
Thank you.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked: The text book Navigating Linux is written after the course restructuring and should feel coherent with the current structure without skipping over topics, feel free to go through it. You may not go through it top to bottom, just open a random section which you feel lost in and read that to understand it better. (This advice applies to most books, not just this).
